title: Hybrid cast allocator and attention-stride scheduler for quant-friendly prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
We observe non-trivial per-token overhead when switching between quantized (INT8/FP8) execution and float32 decode stages, especially at small microbatch sizes and when attention kv cache alignment differs between prefill and decode. Dequantization latency and extra memory copies show up as 8-18% p95 tail regressions on some workloads.

Goal:
Design and implement a hybrid cast allocator and attention-stride scheduler that: (1) minimizes dequant casts during prefill/decode boundary transitions, (2) aligns attention KV layouts to avoid extra transposes/copies, and (3) incorporates an attention-stride-aware scheduling policy so we can run mixed-precision kernels without violating latency SLOs. Target measurable improvements: reduce dequant overhead by >=40% on representative workloads and improve p95 latency by >=10% for short-sequence generation workloads on dedicated GPUs.

Scope and constraints:
- Work targets both INT8 and FP8 execution paths as first-class; mixed-precision fallbacks to FP16/FP32 must be safe and predictable.
- Must integrate with existing prefill/decode scheduling pipeline and KV-caching layer; aim for minimal API surface changes.
- Prioritize GPU kernels for Ampere/Blackwell and NVIDIA Hopper families; maintain sensible behavior on other hardware without regressions.
- Keep changes incremental to allow canary rollout and easy rollback.

Design summary:
1) Hybrid cast allocator: pool of preallocated buffers that can present both quantized and float views without copying via metadata-based reinterpretation plus on-demand lazy dequant only when a true float-op is required. When a kernel supports in-place quant-to-float views, allocator returns zero-copy view.
2) Attention-stride scheduler: track per-request attention stride (kv row-major vs column-major, head ordering) and route to kernels that accept the layout or trigger a single fused layout transform upstream (amortized). Maintain a small layout-compatibility cache keyed by model version + sequence length distribution.
3) Mixed-precision decision logic: runtime policy module that chooses between INT8/FP8/FP16 based on SLO target (latency vs cost), current GPU occupancy, KV cache hit rate, and microbatch composition. Policy exposes per-model knobs and an automated suggestion engine (to be picked up later by Optimize).
4) Prefill-decode boundary optimization: allow prefill to emit quantized KV that decode can consume via lazy casts; add an optional streaming path that decodes a prefix while prefill continues aggregating KV for the next tokens to reduce stall time.

Measurement plan:
- Benchmarks: short-seq chat (prefill 32 tokens, decode 1-4 tokens), single-request high-throughput streaming, and dedicated throughput tests with burst traffic.
- Metrics: p50/p95 generation latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory usage, number of explicit dequant/copy calls per token.
- Baselines: runtime-1.19 and current canary with existing quant paths.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1: Profiling and microbench prototypes (this ticket) -> gated by perf tests.
Phase 2: Kernel integration + allocator (runtime-1.20 alpha).
Phase 3: Canary on low-traffic pool; monitor tracing and rollback window.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Some models require layout transforms that are expensive; mitigation: fused layout transforms only when amortized across >N tokens, otherwise route to safe FP16 kernel.
- Risk: Increased allocator complexity causing memory fragmentation; mitigation: simple pool size heuristics and telemetry to tune.
- Risk: Unexpected numerical regressions on FP8 paths; mitigation: add per-model eval runs and regression alerts in Console.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Hybrid cast allocator prototype integrated into prefill path with an API flag to opt-in
End-to-end benchmark showing >=40% reduction in measured dequant/copy time per token on representative INT8 workloads compared to baseline
p95 latency improvement of >=10% on short-sequence generation workloads in lab canary environment
No numeric regressions >0.5% measured on customer-facing eval prompt set for FP8/INT8 paths
End-to-end unit and integration tests for allocator behavior and layout transforms added to CI
Design doc and rollout plan reviewed and approved by runtime and ML infra leads

Add attention-stride metadata propagation and small compatibility cache
Create mixed-precision policy module and expose model-level override flag
Instrument telemetry: count dequant ops, copies, allocator hits/misses, layout transforms
Run microbenchmarked comparisons across INT8/FP8/FP16 paths and collect results
Write integration tests and e2e perf harness for canary deployment
Draft rollout playbook and add to runbook for rapid rollback
